# Mola UI

> A design system cut like a mola: flat layers, hard keylines, revealed bands. React components for dense internal tools and AI-native interfaces. Published as `@demogar/mola-ui`: React 19, Base UI for behaviour, Tailwind v4 for styling, design tokens as CSS custom properties.

Install and set up:

```bash
npm install @demogar/mola-ui @base-ui/react @fontsource-variable/archivo @fontsource-variable/alegreya @fontsource-variable/martian-mono
```

```tsx
import '@fontsource-variable/archivo/wdth.css'
import '@fontsource-variable/alegreya/wght.css'
import '@fontsource-variable/martian-mono/wdth.css'
import '@demogar/mola-ui/styles.css'
import { Button } from '@demogar/mola-ui'
```

Theme and density are attributes, not props: `<html data-theme="dark" data-density="compact">`. Already on Tailwind v4? Import `@demogar/mola-ui/tailwind.css` into your own build instead of `styles.css`. For right-to-left, set `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` and wrap the app in `DirectionProvider`.

## Rules

- Interactive edges use `shadow-cut` (or `shadow-floating` on overlays), never `border`. `border-keyline` is for decorative dividers only. A box-shadow edge can grow a revealed band on hover without moving its neighbours, and the named utilities keep an outline in forced-colours mode.
- Radius is zero. `rounded-full` only for something that is genuinely a dot. The system is cut cloth: nothing in it is rounded.
- State is never colour alone: glyph, word and colour, in that order of importance. It has to survive colour blindness, a greyscale screenshot and forced colours.
- Disabled is stated, not faded. No `opacity-*` on a disabled control. Opacity fades the keyline and the label to about 2:1, a failure axe does not report because disabled controls are exempt.
- Colours come from tokens. No hex, rgb or arbitrary colour values outside `tokens.css`. Every token pairing has a measured contrast ratio in both themes; a colour outside the token file was never measured.
- Theme and density are attributes (`data-theme`, `data-density`) on `<html>` or a subtree, not props or React context. Dialogs and menus portal to `<body>` and must inherit them. No component takes a density prop.
- Lay out with logical properties: `ps-`/`pe-`, `ms-`/`me-`, `inset-s-`/`inset-e-`, `text-start`/`text-end`. `dir="rtl"` then mirrors the layout with no second set of classes.
- Typefaces have roles: Archivo (`font-ui`) for the interface, Alegreya (`font-text`) for prose from a person or a model, Martian Mono (`literal`) only for machine literals. A reader can tell from the letterforms whether the product, a person or the machine is speaking.
- Labels are sentence case; buttons start with a verb and name the object (“Cancel run”, not “OK”). A button that names its consequence can be chosen without reading the surrounding text.
- Unknown duration is the relleno working state, never a spinner; elapsed time counts up instead of a progress bar inventing a percentage. Model work has no knowable total, and a bar that stalls at 90% is a lie.
- Anything that writes to the world waits for a person, with the choices given equal weight (`ToolCall` approval, `ChangeReview`). An agent’s action is only as safe as the decision in front of it.
- Use the components for behaviour. Do not re-implement focus trapping, roving focus or typeahead; the components are built on Base UI. A maintained primitive gets keyboard and screen-reader behaviour right in more cases than a local copy.

## Actions

### Button

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-actions-button--overview

A cut-shape button for an action on this page, with IconButton for an action shown as an icon alone.

When to use:
- Starting an action: run, save, delete, cancel.
- Primary for the main action of a panel, secondary for the rest, danger only for destruction, ghost for the least emphasis.
- Work in flight after a press, with loading, which keeps the label and adds the working strip instead of a spinner.
- Icon-only actions in dense rows and toolbars, with IconButton and its required label.

When not to:
- Going to another page or URL. Use a link: an a element, or your router’s link styled with buttonVariants.
- A row of related actions above a table or canvas, with one tab stop. Use Toolbar.
- More actions on one object than deserve a button each. Use Menu.
- Choosing between views, where the pressed state stays. Use Segmented control.

- Do: Keep one primary button per panel, and keep danger for actions that destroy something.
- Don’t: Use danger red for emphasis, or set several primary buttons side by side.
- Do: Let a disabled button keep its stated look, and say nearby why it is unavailable.
- Don’t: Fade a button with opacity, or disable it with no explanation.

Content:
- Start with a verb and name the object: “Delete run”, “Start run”, not “OK”, “Yes” or “Submit”.
- Write labels in sentence case with no trailing period; the button sets them in capitals itself.
- Give IconButton a label that names the action and the object, “Copy run id”; it is also the tooltip.

#### `Button` (component)

- `variant`: `primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, `ghost` (default `primary`)
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Leading icon. Decorative: the label is the accessible name. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Work is in flight. The label stays (so the button never changes width mid-click), a strip of working relleno runs along its foot, and the button stops accepting presses while staying focusable and announced as busy. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  |  |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "danger" \| "ghost"` |  |  |
| `withArrow` | `boolean` | `false` | Trailing arrow that slides 3px on hover — for actions that move you somewhere. |

Also accepts the props of `ButtonProps`, `NativeButtonProps`.

#### `ButtonArrow` (component)

The arrow micro-interaction, exported so a router `<Link>` styled with `buttonVariants` gets the same one.

- `variant`: `primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, `ghost` (default `primary`)
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default `md`)

#### `IconButton` (component)

A square button that carries only an icon. `label` is required and becomes the accessible name and the native tooltip, because an icon-only control with no name is the single most common accessibility failure in tool UIs.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The accessible name. Required: an icon is not a label. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Work is in flight. The label stays (so the button never changes width mid-click), a strip of working relleno runs along its foot, and the button stops accepting presses while staying focusable and announced as busy. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md" \| null` |  |  |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| null` |  |  |

Also accepts the props of `ButtonProps`, `NativeButtonProps`.

#### `buttonVariants` (function)

A button is a cut shape, so its edge is a `box-shadow` keyline rather than a `border`. The signature hover reveals a band of the layer beneath the shape, which means the edge has to grow by several pixels without moving anything around it. A border would reflow the toolbar; a shadow does not.

Types: `ButtonProps`, `IconButtonProps`

## Data display

### Avatar

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-data-display-avatar--overview

A person or an agent as a square tile, with initials or a glyph on a colour picked from the name.

When to use:
- Showing who did something in a log, a page header or a list of reviewers.
- Marking an agent with a glyph through icon, so a person and a bot are never confused.
- Several people in one place, with AvatarGroup, which folds the rest into a “+n” tile past max.

When not to:
- Stating a status or a role. Use Badge.
- An image or chart slot that has nothing in it yet. Use Placeholder.

- Do: Pass the full name; it becomes the accessible name and seeds the colour.
- Don’t: Pass initials or a handle as the name; a screen reader then announces “AP”.

Content:
- Name people by full name and agents as people know them: “Support triage”.
- Name an AvatarGroup by role: “Reviewers”, “On call”.

#### `Avatar` (component)

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | The person's or agent's name. Becomes the accessible name and seeds the colour. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown instead of initials when there is no image — e.g. a bot glyph for an agent. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` |  |  |
| `src` | `string` |  |  |

#### `AvatarGroup` (component)

Overlapping tiles, each separated from the next by a ring of the page ground inside its keyline — the gap a blade leaves between two shapes cut from the same layer. Without it, overlapping squares merge into one shape and the count is unreadable.

- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the group: "Reviewers", "On call". |
| `max` | `number` | `4` | Show at most this many; the rest collapse into a "+n" tile. |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `md` |  |

#### `avatarLayer` (function)

#### `avatarVariants` (function)

#### `initials` (function)

Types: `AvatarGroupProps`, `AvatarProps`

### Code

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-data-display-code--overview

Machine text: Code for an inline literal, CodeBlock for a labelled block with copy and wrap.

When to use:
- An id, a field name or a flag inside a sentence, with Code.
- A tool’s arguments, a query or a log tail, with CodeBlock; JSON is tokenised by value kind.
- A payload cut off mid-stream; CodeBlock shows exactly what arrived.

When not to:
- Figures compared down a column, such as cost and duration; they are Archivo with tabular figures. Use Meta.
- A keyboard shortcut. Use Kbd.
- A proposed change to a file, shown as additions and removals. Use Change review.
- Labels, headings or emphasis; the monospace is only for text a machine reads. Use Text.

- Do: Use Code for a literal inside a sentence.
- Don’t: Break a sentence with a CodeBlock to show one id.
- Do: Turn copyable off for payloads that must not leave the page.
- Don’t: Put a CodeBlock on a black terminal panel; it sits on the same cloth as everything else.

Content:
- Show literals exactly as the system stores them; do not change their case or add spaces.
- Label a CodeBlock by its role or file name, as the reader would search for it: “arguments”, “query.sql”.

#### `Code` (component)

An inline machine literal: an id, a field name, a flag.

#### `CodeBlock` (component)

A block of machine text — a tool call's arguments, a query, a log tail.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | Hide the copy button — for payloads that must not leave the page. |
| `label` | `string` |  | A filename or a role — "arguments", "result", "query.sql". |
| `language` | `CodeLanguage` | `text` | Shown as a tag in the header. Only `json` is tokenized; everything else is plain. |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `maxHeight` | `string` |  | Scroll inside after this height (any CSS length). |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | Start with long lines wrapped. The reader can toggle it. |

#### `tokenizeJson` (function)

#### `JSON_TOKEN_CLASS` (constant)

Types: `CodeBlockProps`, `CodeLanguage`, `JsonToken`, `JsonTokenKind`

### Description list

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-data-display-description-list--overview

Term and value pairs: the properties of a run, a document or an evaluation.

When to use:
- A side panel of properties scanned top to bottom, with the inline layout.
- Values long enough to wrap, such as a system prompt or a path, with the stacked layout.
- A summary that closes a section, with the grid layout.
- Ids, hashes and model names marked literal, so they are never read as prose.

When not to:
- Many records with the same fields, compared row against row. Use Table.
- A few headline figures with their change over time. Use Stat.
- The fields of a record before and after a proposed change. Use FieldChanges.

- Do: Mark ids and model strings literal, and leave prose and figures in the system voice.
- Don’t: Set every value in the monospace.

Content:
- Terms are short nouns in sentence case, without colons: “Model”, “Duration”.
- Give values their units, “41s”, “$0.2185”, and show a status as a Badge rather than a bare word.

#### `DescriptionList` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `DescriptionItem[]` |  |  |
| `layout` | `"grid" \| "inline" \| "stacked" \| null` | `inline` |  |

Types: `DescriptionItem`, `DescriptionListProps`

### Stat

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-data-display-stat--overview

A KPI tile: a label, a figure, a change with its direction and sentiment, and an optional sparkline.

When to use:
- Headline figures at the top of a page, grouped in a StatGroup cut from one panel.
- A change whose direction and meaning differ, such as latency going down being good news.
- The shape of the recent past as a sparkline beside the figure.

When not to:
- A reading against a limit or threshold, such as a quota. Use Meter.
- Many properties of one object. Use Description list.
- A trend that needs axes, values or several series. A sparkline is a glyph; use a chart.

- Do: State direction and sentiment separately, so cost going down reads as good.
- Don’t: Assume up is green; latency going up is a regression.

Content:
- The label names the measure and its window: “Runs today”, “p95 duration”.
- Put the unit in unit, “%”, and the comparison in the delta’s period, “vs yesterday”.
- Group digits and keep only the precision a reader uses: “1,204”, “97.8”.

#### `Sparkline` (component)

An ink polyline — no fill, no gradient, no axis. A sparkline is the shape of the recent past and nothing more; the moment it grows a gridline it is a chart pretending to be a glyph. The last point is a square cut out in rojo (it is the "now" the figure beside it states), drawn as a square because a blade does not cut circles.

#### `Stat` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `value` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `delta` | `StatDelta` |  |  |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` |  | A line of context under the figure. |
| `trend` | `number[]` |  | The recent series, oldest first. Drawn in ink with the latest point cut out in rojo. |
| `unit` | `ReactNode` |  | Set smaller beside the figure: "ms", "runs", "%". |

#### `StatGroup` (component)

Tiles cut from one panel rather than four floating cards: one ink keyline around the group, decorative keylines between tiles. Four separate cut shapes in a row would put eight ink edges where the eye needs one.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `4` | Columns at the widest breakpoint. Tiles wrap down to two, then one. |

Types: `StatDelta`, `StatGroupProps`, `StatProps`

### Table

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--overview

Table primitives for rows of records, and DataTable for columns as data with sorting, selection, column visibility and pages.

When to use:
- Comparing many records with the same fields, such as runs, documents or evaluations.
- Sorting, selection, bulk actions and pages on client or server data, with DataTable.
- A layout DataTable does not cover, such as virtualised rows, with the primitives.

When not to:
- The properties of one record. Use Description list.
- Events where the order is the content. Use Timeline.
- A handful of headline figures. Use Stat.

- Do: Right-align numeric columns, header included, in tabular figures.
- Don’t: Left-align costs and durations, or set them in the monospace.
- Do: Show the no-results empty row with Clear filters when filters hide every row.
- Don’t: Tell someone to create their first run when a filter is hiding the runs they have.

Content:
- Headers are short nouns in sentence case: “Run”, “Started”, “Cost”.
- Show a value that does not exist yet as an em dash, “—”, not as zero.
- Set noun so counts read naturally: “3 runs selected”.

#### `Table` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frameClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the scrolling frame, e.g. `max-h-96`. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `false` | Bound the table with a keyline on a raised ground — for a table that is the panel. |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the header row visible while the body scrolls. Give the frame a height via `frameClassName`. |

#### `TableBody` (component)

#### `TableCaption` (component)

#### `TableCell` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `numeric` | `boolean` | `false` | Right-aligned tabular figures. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` | `false` | Cut long content to one line with an ellipsis. The full text goes in `title` when the content is a string, so it is never lost — only folded. |

#### `TableCheckbox` (component)

A native checkbox, drawn as a cut square. Native, so space toggles it, forms submit it and screen readers announce it with no ARIA to keep in sync; the visible square is a sibling painted from the input's own `:checked` and `:indeterminate` state.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | Some but not all rows are selected. A DOM property, not an attribute, so it is set by effect. |

#### `TableEmpty` (component)

The empty state, as a row. It spans the table rather than replacing it, so the headers stay and the reader still knows what would have been here.

#### `TableFooter` (component)

#### `TableHead` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `numeric` | `boolean` | `false` | Right-align, for a column of figures. Header and cells must agree or the label floats off its numbers. |
| `onSort` | `(() => void)` |  |  |
| `sort` | `SortDirection` |  | Makes the header a sort control. `none` renders the control in its idle state; `aria-sort` is only set on the column actually sorted, because announcing "not sorted" on every column is noise. |

#### `TableHeader` (component)

#### `TableRow` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | The row is part of the current selection. Gold, because gold is the layer this system marks a choice with — it is also the text-selection colour — while añil stays free to mean "information". The fill is a wash, not the layer, so every ink in the row still clears AA; and an ink bar on the leading edge carries the state for anyone who cannot see the hue. |

#### `TableSkeletonRows` (component)

Loading rows: real rows at the real height, so the table does not jump when the data lands. Bar widths vary by a fixed pattern rather than at random, so a re-render does not make the skeleton twitch.

#### `DataTable` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` (required) | `DataTableColumn<Row>[]` |  |  |

| `bulkActions` | `((context: DataTableBulkContext) => ReactNode)` |  | Actions for the selected rows, shown in the bar above the table while any are selected. |

| `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` |  |
| `defaultSelection` | `Iterable<string>` |  |  |
| `defaultSort` | `DataTableSort` |  |  |
| `empty` | `ReactNode \| DataTableEmpty` |  |  |
| `frameClassName` | `string` |  |  |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `false` |  |

| `label` | `string` |  | Names the table for assistive tech when there is no visible caption. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |  |

| `sort` | `DataTableSort \| null` |  | Controlled sort. `null` is "no sort"; leave undefined to let the table own it. |
| `stickyHeader` | `boolean` | `false` |  |

#### `DataTableColumnMenu` (component)

Which columns show. Toggling does not close the menu, because columns are chosen several at a time. The last visible column cannot be hidden — a table with no columns is not a state worth being able to reach — and a column marked `hideable: false` is shown checked and disabled, so the menu still says it exists.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` (required) | `DataTableColumn<Row>[]` |  |  |
| `hidden` (required) | `ReadonlySet<string>` |  |  |
| `onToggle` (required) | `(key: string, visible: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

Types: `TableCellProps`, `TableCheckboxProps`, `TableHeadProps`, `TableProps`, `TableRowProps`, `DataTableBulkContext`, `DataTableColumn`, `DataTableColumnMenuProps`, `DataTableEmpty`, `DataTableProps`, `DataTableSort`, `SortValue`

### Timeline

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-data-display-timeline--overview

Timeline for events already written down, on a spine; StepList for ordered steps a person follows.

When to use:
- An audit log, a deploy history or the stages of an evaluation, with Timeline.
- A runbook or a checklist, with StepList and its ruled bands.
- The event happening now, with the active tone and its working relleno.

When not to:
- A live agent run whose steps change as it works. Use Agent run.
- Records compared by their fields rather than read in order. Use Table.
- Sections of one document that open and close. Use Accordion.

- Do: Put when or where in meta, and what happened in the title.
- Don’t: Leave the node colour to say what happened; the words have to carry it.

Content:
- Timeline titles state the event in the past tense: “Review approved”, “Rollout paused”.
- StepList titles are instructions: “Freeze the agent version”.
- Use one time format down the list: “Oct 1 · 09:12”.

#### `StepList` (component)

Ruled, ordered steps — a runbook, an onboarding checklist, the stages of a rollout. Where `Timeline` is a spine with a node per event, this is a stack of ruled bands with a label column, and merging the two would mean a component whose every rule is conditional.

- `tone`: `default`, `inverse`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "inverse"` | `default` | `inverse` sets the list on an ink panel. |

#### `Timeline` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `TimelineItem[]` |  |  |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the list, since the spine carries no heading of its own. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `gap` | `"spaced" \| "flush"` | `spaced` | `spaced`   separate events, a gap between rows. `flush`    one continuous journey, carried by the connector alone. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "editorial"` | `default` | `default`   product scale: semibold titles at body size. `editorial` the travel-guide scale it was born at, for a narrative. |
| `titleAs` | `"h3" \| "h4" \| "p"` | `p` | The element each title renders as. Defaults to a non-heading, since most logs are not outlines. |

Types: `StepListItem`, `TimelineItem`, `TimelineProps`, `TimelineTone`

## Feedback

### Badge

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-badge--overview

A small status mark in one of the system’s tones; StatusDot for a square dot beside a label; RecommendationBadge for an editorial scale.

When to use:
- The state of a row or an object: queued, live, failed, pinned.
- Soft by default; solid for the one state on a row that must be seen first; outline for categories.
- A state that is live right now, with pulse, which stills under reduced motion.

When not to:
- The state of a run, a step or a tool call; model work has its own vocabulary. Use Run status.
- A message with a sentence and an action. Use Callout.
- A filter a person turns on and off. Use Chip.
- A count on a tab; tabs and navigation items take count themselves. Use Tabs.

- Do: Give every badge a word, and every StatusDot a label beside it or its own label.
- Don’t: Let a coloured dot alone carry a state.
- Do: Use soft badges down a column.
- Don’t: Fill a column with solid badges; fifty solid statuses read as a quilt.

Content:
- One or two words in sentence case, with no punctuation: “Succeeded”, “Needs review”.
- Use the same status words as the filters and headers around it.

#### `Badge` (component)

- `tone`: `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warn`, `danger`, `accent` (default `neutral`)
- `variant`: `solid`, `soft`, `outline` (default `soft`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dot` | `boolean` | `false` | A leading StatusDot in the badge's tone. |
| `pulse` | `boolean` | `false` | Pulse the dot — for a state that is live right now (running, streaming). |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warn" \| "danger" \| "accent"` |  |  |
| `variant` | `"solid" \| "soft" \| "outline"` |  |  |

#### `RecommendationBadge` (component)

- `level`: `essential`, `highly`, `detour`, `time` (default `essential`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `"essential" \| "highly" \| "detour" \| "time"` |  |  |

#### `StatusDot` (component)

A square, not a circle. It is a scrap of cut cloth, and a round dot is the one shape a blade cannot make. Gold dots carry an ink keyline because gold on light cloth is 1.66:1 — under the 3:1 a graphic mark needs to be seen.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` |  | Announced text for a dot used on its own. Omit when the dot sits beside a label that already says the state — then it is decorative and hidden. |
| `pulse` | `boolean` | `false` | The state is live. Respects reduced motion: the pulse stills, the dot stays. |
| `tone` | `BadgeTone` | `neutral` |  |

#### `RECOMMENDATION_LABELS` (constant)

#### `badgeVariants` (function)

A status mark. Small, flat, cut — a scrap of the layer that says what state something is in.

#### `recommendationVariants` (function)

The editorial recommendation scale from Must Do Panama, where this system was born — kept as lineage, and because "how strongly do we stand behind this" is a scale a growth or knowledge tool also has. Gold is the layer a mola reveals last and least, so gold is `essential`.

Types: `BadgeProps`, `BadgeTone`, `RecommendationBadgeProps`, `RecommendationLevel`, `StatusDotProps`

### Callout

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-callout--overview

A message that belongs to a region of the page, with a tone, an optional title and actions.

When to use:
- A standing condition of a page or panel: a model that retires soon, a read-only workspace, a stale index.
- Something to read before working in the region, with one or two actions.
- A notice the person can dismiss, with onDismiss, where the caller decides whether it returns.

When not to:
- Something that has just happened, possibly elsewhere, such as a finished re-index. Use Toast.
- A decision the person must make before going on. Use AlertDialog.
- A panel with nothing to show. Use Empty state.
- A short status on a row. Use Badge.

- Do: Match the tone to the consequence: warn for a limit approaching, danger for something broken.
- Don’t: Use danger for news or tips; red has to keep meaning broken.
- Do: Put a callout that appears after an action inside a live region, or use a toast.
- Don’t: Insert a static callout after an action and expect a screen reader to notice it.

Content:
- The title states the condition: “Token budget at 86%”, not “Warning” or “Heads up”.
- The body says what it means and what to do: “Switch the model in settings to keep evaluation history comparable.”
- Actions are verbs on the object: “Retry from 812”, “View log”.

#### `Callout` (component)

- `tone`: `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warn`, `danger` (default `info`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons under the body. Usually one secondary, at `size="sm"`. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `3` | The heading element for `title`. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Replace the tone's default icon, or `false` for none. |
| `onDismiss` | `(() => void)` |  | Renders a dismiss button. The caller owns whether it comes back. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warn" \| "danger"` |  |  |

#### `calloutVariants` (function)

A message that belongs to a region of the page — "this agent is using a deprecated model", "billing is in read-only mode" — rather than to a moment, which is a toast's job.

Types: `CalloutProps`, `CalloutTone`

### Empty state

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-empty-state--overview

What a panel shows when it has nothing to show, in four variants: empty, no results, error and no permission.

When to use:
- Nothing exists yet, and the action creates the first one.
- Filters hide everything, and the action clears them.
- The panel could not load, and the action retries.
- The content exists but is not the reader’s to see, and the text says who can grant it.

When not to:
- Content that is on its way. Use Skeleton.
- One slot, such as a chart or an image, waiting for its content. Use Placeholder.
- A warning about a page that does have content. Use Callout.
- A table with no rows; the table’s own empty row keeps the headers. Use Table.

- Do: Pick the variant for the conversation: no-results says filters are hiding things, and clears them.
- Don’t: Tell someone filtering their runs to “create your first run”.
- Do: Say who can grant access in no-permission.
- Don’t: Show “Access denied” with no next step.

Content:
- The title states the condition: “No runs match these filters”, “Traces did not load”.
- The description gives the cause or the count: “3 filters are hiding 1,284 runs.”
- An error says what happened and what happens next: “The trace store returned 503. This panel will try again in 30s.”

#### `EmptyState` (component)

- `variant`: `empty`, `no-results`, `error`, `no-permission` (default `empty`)
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | One or two buttons. The first is the way forward. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4` | `3` |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  | Replace the variant's icon, or `false` for none. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  |  |
| `variant` | `"empty" \| "no-results" \| "error" \| "no-permission"` |  |  |

#### `emptyStateVariants` (function)

The state a panel is in when it has nothing to show — designed as a condition rather than as an apology.

Types: `EmptyStateProps`

### Placeholder

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-placeholder--overview

A slot for something that does not exist yet, such as a chart with no data, announced as one image.

When to use:
- A chart, preview or image that cannot render yet, held at its final size.
- A layout where the slot must keep its place, with a label for the kind of thing and a name for what it would show.

When not to:
- Content that is loading and will arrive shortly. Use Skeleton.
- A whole panel with nothing in it, which needs an action. Use Empty state.
- A person or agent without a photo; initials stand in. Use Avatar.

Content:
- label is the kind, “Chart” or “Preview”; name is the thing, “Retention by cohort”.
- alt says what is missing, “No data yet: run latency by agent”, because it is announced in place of the content.

#### `Placeholder` (component)

The slot where something will go and has not yet: a photograph that has not been shot, a chart with no data, a preview that cannot render.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alt` (required) | `string` |  | Announced in place of the missing content. |
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | What it would show — "Panama Canal", "Retention by cohort". |
| `label` | `string` | `Placeholder` | The kind of thing that goes here — "Photography", "Chart", "Preview". |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "deep"` | `default` |  |

Types: `PlaceholderProps`

### Progress

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-progress--overview

Progress for work moving toward done, which may be indeterminate; Meter for a reading inside a known range, with thresholds.

When to use:
- An upload, an ingest or an evaluation over a known number of items, with Progress.
- Work that has started but has no known size yet, with a null value: the working relleno, not a spinner.
- A budget, a quota or a context window, with Meter and its warn and danger thresholds.

When not to:
- A model call or an agent run with no knowable total; show elapsed time, not a percentage. Use Run status.
- Content loading into a known layout. Use Skeleton.
- A headline figure with no range. Use Stat.
- Choosing a value on a scale. Use Slider.

- Do: Use Meter for a reading that can go down as well as up, such as tokens used this month.
- Don’t: Use Progress for a quota; a quota is not work moving toward done.
- Do: Use valueText to give the count: “212 / 300”.
- Don’t: Invent a percentage to make a wait feel shorter.

Content:
- Progress labels name the work as it happens: “Embedding documents”, “Evaluating prompts”.
- A bar that stays on screen after the work ends says how it ended: “Failed at 67%”.
- Meter labels name the measure and its period: “Tokens this month”.

#### `Meter` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
| `thresholds` | `{ warn?: number; danger?: number; } \| undefined` | `{ warn: 0.75, danger: 0.9 }` | Fractions of the range at which the fill changes: gold past `warn`, rojo past `danger`. Drawn on the track as ticks. Pass `{}` for none. |
| `valueText` | `((formatted: string, value: number) => ReactNode)` |  |  |

Also accepts the props of `MeterRootProps`.

#### `Progress` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Visible label; also the accessible name. Use `aria-label` when there is no room for one. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the formatted value at the end of the label row. Ignored while indeterminate. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
| `tone` | `"danger" \| "success" \| "ink"` | `ink` | Fill colour. Ink is in-flight; verde/rojo for a finished state that stays on screen. |
| `valueText` | `((formatted: string \| null, value: number \| null) => ReactNode)` |  | Replaces the value text, e.g. "212 / 300 prompts". |

Also accepts the props of `ProgressRootProps`.

#### `meterLevel` (function)

Which band a reading is in — exported for the stat tiles and tables that colour a number to match.

Types: `MeterProps`, `ProgressProps`

### Skeleton

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-skeleton--overview

Bones in the shape of content that has not arrived, with SkeletonGroup to mark the region busy and say once what is loading.

When to use:
- A card, list or table whose layout is known while its data loads.
- Swapping bones for content in place, so the layout barely moves when the data lands.
- Lines of text that follow the surrounding type size, with SkeletonText.

When not to:
- Work with a known size, such as an upload. Use Progress.
- A slot whose content does not exist yet, rather than one that is loading. Use Placeholder.
- A button waiting on its own action; give it its loading state. Use Button.
- Text a model is still writing. Use Streaming text.

- Do: Wrap the bones in SkeletonGroup with a label, so the region is announced once.
- Don’t: Add a spinner or a “Loading…” line to each bone; the system has no spinner, by design.
- Do: Cut the bones to the content’s shape: an avatar bone, a short line for a name.
- Don’t: Cover the area with one generic block.

Content:
- The group label names what is loading: “Loading agent”, “Loading runs”.

#### `Skeleton` (component)

Loading is a cut shape whose content has not arrived, so a block keeps the keyline every other shape has and carries the same relleno as the empty state.

- `shape`: `block`, `text`, `line`, `avatar` (default `block`)
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `"block" \| "text" \| "line" \| "avatar"` |  |  |
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` |  |  |

#### `SkeletonGroup` (component)

The region that is loading, and the one place that says so.

- `shape`: `block`, `text`, `line`, `avatar` (default `block`)
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fallback` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The bones, shown while loading. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What is loading, said once: "Loading agent", "Loading runs". |
| `loading` (required) | `boolean` |  | While true the bones show and the region is busy. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The real content, shown once loaded. |

#### `SkeletonText` (component)

Lines of text that have not arrived. The last line is short, because a paragraph ends ragged; a block of equal bars reads as a table.

- `shape`: `block`, `text`, `line`, `avatar` (default `block`)
- `size`: `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` (default `md`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `number` | `3` |  |

Types: `SkeletonGroupProps`, `SkeletonProps`, `SkeletonTextProps`

### Toast

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-feedback-toast--overview

A floating notice for something that happened elsewhere or just now; a running toast turns into its result in place.

When to use:
- Confirming an action whose result is not visible where the operator is.
- Long work the operator may leave, with toast.running, then toast.update with the outcome.
- One follow-up action, such as Undo or View run.

When not to:
- A condition of the page that stays true, such as read-only mode. Use Callout.
- Anything that needs a decision, or more than one action. Use Dialog.
- A validation error on a field. Use Field.
- Confirming a copy to the clipboard. Confirm it in place, as CodeBlock and Message do.

- Do: Update the running toast with the outcome, so the result lands where the work was.
- Don’t: Leave the running toast and fire a second, unrelated success toast.

Content:
- The title states what happened, in the past tense: “Index rebuilt”, “Deploy failed”.
- The description adds the cause or the figures: “1,204 documents · 3m 41s”.
- The action is one verb: “Undo”, “Retry”, “View”.

#### `ToastProvider` (component)

Mount once near the root. Renders the viewport, bottom-right, into a portal.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `number` | `3` | Toasts kept visible at once; older ones fold away. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `5000` | Default auto-dismiss, ms. |

#### `useToast` (hook)

The toast API. Call from anywhere inside a `ToastProvider`.

Types: `ToastOptions`, `ToastProviderProps`, `ToastTone`

## Forms

### Checkbox

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-checkbox--overview

A square that turns a choice on or off, applied when the form is saved; CheckboxGroup for any number of choices from a set.

When to use:
- One yes-or-no setting that takes effect on Save.
- Any number of options from a short visible list, with CheckboxGroup and its legend.
- A parent that selects all its children, and goes indeterminate when only some are on.

When not to:
- A setting that takes effect the moment it changes. Use Switch.
- Exactly one option from a set. Use Radio.
- Filters above a list that apply as they are pressed. Use Chip.
- A long list of options that people would rather search. Use Combobox.

- Do: Label the positive choice: “Stream partial output”.
- Don’t: Label a negative, “Don’t stream output”, which makes checked mean off.

Content:
- Labels state what is turned on, in sentence case, with no trailing period.
- Conditions go in description, not in the label: “Up to three times, with exponential backoff.”
- The legend names the set: “Tools”, “Notify on”.

#### `Checkbox` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Second line under the label. Linked as the control's description. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Visible label. The whole label is the press target. |

Also accepts the props of `CheckboxRootProps`, `NativeButtonProps`.

#### `CheckboxGroup` (component)

A set of checkboxes that share one value array, inside a real fieldset and legend — so a screen reader announces "Tools, group" before the first option and every option is heard in that context, which no `aria-label` on a div reproduces across readers.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The group's name, rendered as the fieldset legend in the label register. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Copy under the legend. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` | Lay options out in a row rather than a column. |

Also accepts the props of `CheckboxGroupProps`.

#### `checkboxBoxClasses` (constant)

A square cut from the cloth. Unchecked, it is raised cloth inside an ink keyline; checked, the square is filled with ink and the mark is cut out of it in cloth — the same inversion a selected chip and a selected segment make, so "on" looks the same wherever it appears.

Types: `CheckboxGroupProps`, `CheckboxProps`

### Chip

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-chip--overview

A filter chip with a real checkbox or radio inside, filled with ink when on, with an optional count.

When to use:
- Filters above a list or table that apply as they are pressed.
- Showing how many rows each filter would leave, with count.
- One of a few fixed ranges, such as 1h, 24h and 7d, with type set to radio.

When not to:
- A status shown to the reader rather than chosen by them. Use Badge.
- Switching between views of the same data. Use Segmented control.
- Options in a form that is saved later. Use Checkbox.
- Values picked from a long list into a field; Combobox shows them as chips inside it. Use Combobox.

- Do: Wrap chips in a ChipGroup with a legend, so “Failed” is heard as a status filter.
- Don’t: Leave a row of chips unnamed; “Failed” on its own sounds like an error.

Content:
- Use the same words as the status being filtered: “Succeeded”, “Failed”.
- Keep default chips to one line; use the comfortable size for labels that wrap.

#### `Chip` (component)

- `size`: `default`, `comfortable` (default `default`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label. Also the control's accessible name, via the wrapping `<label>`. |
| `count` | `number` |  | A count after the label: how many rows this filter would leave. Tabular, so a row of chips does not jitter as counts change. |
| `size` | `"default" \| "comfortable"` |  |  |
| `type` | `"checkbox" \| "radio"` | `checkbox` | `radio` for one-of-N within a `name` group, `checkbox` for multi-select. |

#### `ChipGroup` (component)

A row of chips inside a real fieldset. The legend is what a screen reader says before the first chip — "Status, group" — so "Failed" is heard as a status filter rather than as an alarming word on its own.

- `size`: `default`, `comfortable` (default `default`)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What the chips filter. Rendered as the legend, so each chip is announced in its context. |
| `hideLegend` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide the legend visually while keeping it for assistive technology — for a toolbar row whose meaning is obvious from position. |

#### `chipVariants` (function)

A filter you can see the state of. A real `<input type="checkbox|radio">` sits inside the styled `<label>`, hidden with the clip pattern (`sr-only`) rather than `display:none`, so it stays focusable and in the accessibility tree. Keyboard handling, radio-group arrow keys, the checked state and form submission all come from the platform — there is no ARIA widget to keep in sync and nothing to re-implement.

Types: `ChipGroupProps`, `ChipProps`

### Combobox

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-combobox--overview

A select you can type into: Combobox always ends on an option from the list; Autocomplete takes free text with suggestions.

When to use:
- A list too long to scroll, such as people, tools or runs, where typing narrows it.
- Several values from a long list, with multiple, shown as chips inside the field.
- A server search, with filter set to null and loading and status reporting the results.
- Free text where suggestions save keystrokes and keep names consistent, such as a run label, with Autocomplete.

When not to:
- A short list people can scan without typing. Use Select.
- Two to five options that should all be visible. Use Radio.
- Jumping to a page or running a command from anywhere. Use Command palette.
- Filtering the rows of a list as you type. Use SearchInput.

- Do: Use Combobox when the form must submit a value the list offered, such as a reviewer.
- Don’t: Use Autocomplete for a reviewer or an owner; a half-typed name would be submitted as typed.
- Do: Write the empty message for the moment: before typing, what can be searched; after, the query that found nothing.
- Don’t: Leave the popup blank while results load or when nothing matches.

Content:
- The placeholder says what to type: “Search people”, “run-4187 or eval-sweeper”.
- Keep a disabled option in the list, with its reason as the description: “Requires approval”.

#### `Autocomplete` (component)

Free text with suggestions: a run label, a tag, a search. The typed text is the value; picking a suggestion only fills it in.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `(string \| ComboboxOption)[]` |  | Suggestions. Plain strings, or options with a description line. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  |  |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `autoComplete` | `string` | `off` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `emptyMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | What the popup says when nothing matches. Omit to close the popup instead. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `locale` | `LocalesArgument` |  | Locale for the built-in matching. Omitted, the runtime's locale is used. |
| `name` | `string` |  |  |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string) => void)` |  | Every change to the text, typed or chosen. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
| `status` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` |  |  |

#### `Combobox` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `Items` |  | Flat options, or labelled groups. With `filter={null}`, the options to show right now. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  |  |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `clearLabel` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the clear button. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `emptyMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | What the popup says when nothing matches. |
| `filter` | `((option: ComboboxOption, query: string) => boolean) \| null` |  | How typed text matches an option. Pass `null` when the caller filters — a server search — and hand the results in through `items`. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | A visible label above the field. Omit it inside `Field`, which renders its own, and spread Field's control props onto this component instead. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Results are on their way: the popup shows the working texture and "Searching…". |
| `locale` | `LocalesArgument` |  | Locale for the built-in matching. Omitted, the runtime's locale is used. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  |  |
| `onInputValueChange` | `((query: string) => void)` |  | What is typed, as it is typed: the hook for a server search. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string \| null) => void) \| ((value: string[]) => void)` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `removeLabel` | `((label: string) => string)` |  | Accessible name of each chip's remove button. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` |  |  |
| `status` | `ReactNode` |  | A line above the results — "Showing 20 of 312", or an error from the search. |
| `triggerLabel` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the button that opens the list. |
| `value` | `string \| string[] \| null` |  |  |

Types: `AutocompleteProps`, `ComboboxMultipleProps`, `ComboboxOption`, `ComboboxOptionGroup`, `ComboboxProps`, `ComboboxSingleProps`

### Date picker

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-date-picker--overview

DatePicker for one date, typed or picked from a calendar; DateRangePicker for a period, with presets and two typed ends.

When to use:
- One date, such as when to run an evaluation, with DatePicker.
- A period for a report or a filter, with DateRangePicker and presets such as the last 7 days.
- Dates with bounds or unavailable days, through min, max and isDateDisabled.

When not to:
- A period between two dates, where two single pickers would not check the order. Use DateRangePicker.
- One date; a range picker would ask for a second press. Use DatePicker.
- A duration, such as a timeout in seconds. Use Number input.
- A few fixed relative ranges, such as 1h, 24h and 7d. Use Chip.

- Do: Pass locale, so the typed order, digits and first day of the week follow it.
- Don’t: Guess the date order from the language; es-ES and es-PA write dates in different orders.
- Do: Keep typed entry on in DateRangePicker; typing is the accessible path into a date.
- Don’t: Turn typedEntry off unless the presets and the grid cover every case.

Content:
- Label the field by what the date is for: “Run evaluation on”, “Report period”.
- Leave the placeholder to the component; it is the locale’s own pattern.
- Rules the picker cannot know, such as required, go to Field as an instruction: “Choose a date for the evaluation.”

#### `Calendar` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activeCellRef` | `Ref<HTMLTableCellElement>` |  | Ref to the day cell that holds the roving tab stop. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Move focus to the active day when the calendar mounts — for a popup that has just opened. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultFocusedDate` | `Date \| null` |  | Where focus starts. Defaults to the selected day, else today. |
| `headingId` | `string` |  | Id for the month heading, so a dialog can be named by it. |
| `isDateDisabled` | `((date: Date) => boolean)` |  | Days that exist but cannot be chosen: weekends in a freeze, public holidays. |
| `locale` | `LocalesArgument` |  | BCP 47 tag. `undefined` uses the runtime's locale, as Intl does. |
| `max` | `Date \| null` |  |  |
| `min` | `Date \| null` |  |  |
| `onSelect` | `((date: Date) => void)` |  | Called with the day a person chose. Range logic belongs to the caller. |
| `renderHeading` | `((props: { id: string; className: string; children: ReactNode; }) => ReactNode)` |  | Render the heading as the popup's title instead of a plain element. |
| `selected` | `DateRange` |  | The selected day, or the range. A single date is a range whose ends match. |
| `today` | `Date` |  | Inject "now" for stable stories and tests. |
| `visibleDate` | `Date \| null` |  | Show this day's month and move the tab stop to it, without moving focus — for a date typed elsewhere that the grid should follow. Compared by identity, so a new `Date` for the same day shows it again after the person has paged away. |
| `weekStartsOn` | `number` |  | 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Overrides the locale's first day of the week. |

| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `isDateDisabled` | `((date: Date) => boolean)` |  |  |
| `locale` | `LocalesArgument` |  |  |
| `max` | `Date \| null` |  |  |

| `required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
| `today` | `Date` |  |  |
| `typedEntry` | `boolean` | `true` | Start and end inputs above the calendar. On by default: typing is the accessible path into a date, not an extra, and the single picker always has it. Turn it off only where presets and the grid cover every case. |
| `value` | `DateRange` |  |  |
| `weekStartsOn` | `number` |  |  |

#### `formatDateRange` (function)

"6 – 12 Oct 2026" in the locale's own words, or null for an incomplete range.

#### `defaultRangePresets` (constant)

The presets an analytics screen reaches for. "Last 7 days" includes today: it is the seven days you can see on the chart, ending now.

#### `getDatePattern` (function)

The typed format for a locale, read from `formatToParts` rather than from a table of locales — so it is right for any locale the engine knows, and the guidance shown under the field can never disagree with what is accepted. The letters are Latin (DD, MM, YYYY) in every locale: it is the convention people recognise as a format, where translated letters are not.

Types: `CalendarProps`, `DatePickerProps`, `DateRangePickerProps`, `DateLocale`, `DatePattern`, `DateRange`, `DateRangePreset`

### Field

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-field--overview

A label, a control and a hint or error wired together; the page also covers Input, Textarea, SearchInput and Label.

When to use:
- Any form control that needs a visible label, a hint and a validation message, through the render prop.
- One line of text with Input, with a unit or an icon inside the field through leading and trailing.
- Several lines with Textarea, which grows with its content when autosize is set.
- Filtering a list with SearchInput, which shows a shortcut cap when empty and a clear button when not.

When not to:
- A number that is stepped, bounded or formatted. Use Number input.
- A choice from a known list. Use Select.
- A date or a period. Use Date picker.
- A prompt to a model, with attachments and a send button. Use Prompt input.

- Do: Spread the control props onto the control, so its id, description and invalid state are wired.
- Don’t: Use the placeholder as the label; it disappears as soon as someone types.
- Do: Put the unit inside the field with trailing: “seconds”, “tokens”.
- Don’t: Write the unit as text after the field, where it reads as a second field.

Content:
- Labels are short nouns in sentence case: “Run name”, “Webhook URL”.
- Hints explain the consequence: “Shown in the run list and in alerts.”
- Errors say what is wrong and how to fix it: “Must be between 1 and 900 seconds.”

#### `Label` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `optional` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the "Optional" tag. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the required asterisk. Does NOT set `required` on any control. |

#### `Field` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Alias of `hint`, for callers who think of it as a description. `hint` wins if both are set. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | Validation message under the control. Its presence is what marks the field invalid. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` |  | Supporting copy under the control. |
| `labelAside` | `ReactNode` |  | Something to the right of the label: a character count, a "Reset" link. |
| `optional` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the "Optional" tag. Ignored when `required`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` |  |

#### `Input` (component)

A text control. Without adornments it is the bare `<input>` wearing the shared control classes; with them, the CUT moves to a wrapper and the input inside goes transparent, so the icon or unit sits inside the same keyline as the text rather than beside it — a unit outside the box reads as a second field.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` |  | Inside the cut, before the text: an icon, a currency sign, a protocol. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` | Height and type from the density tokens. |
| `trailing` | `ReactNode` |  | Inside the cut, after the text: a unit ("ms", "tokens"), a button. |

#### `Textarea` (component)

Multi-line text: a system prompt, a note on a run, a JSON override. Same cut and states as `Input`; padding comes from the density tokens so the first line sits where a single-line input's text would.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autosize` | `boolean` | `false` | Grow with the content instead of scrolling inside a fixed box, using `field-sizing: content` — no script, no resize observer, and it still respects `rows` as the minimum and `max-h-*` as the ceiling. Browsers without it fall back to the normal resizable textarea, which is the correct degradation rather than a broken one. |

#### `SearchInput` (component)

The filter box that heads every list in an internal tool.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clearLabel` | `string` | `Clear search` | Accessible name for the clear button. |
| `onClear` | `(() => void)` |  | Called after the clear button empties the field. |
| `shortcut` | `string` |  | The keyboard shortcut that focuses this field, shown as a key cap while the field is empty — e.g. `⌘K` or `/`. Display only: binding the key is the page's job, because only the page knows what else is listening. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` |  | Height and type from the density tokens. |

#### `fieldControlClasses` (constant)

The one class list every text control shares — Input, Textarea, the Select trigger, and the wrapper an adorned Input draws instead of the input itself.

#### `fieldControlSizes` (constant)

Height, padding and type per size. Every value is a density token, so the same `md` input is 28px in a compact table filter and 48px in a spacious form without a prop changing.

Types: `LabelProps`, `FieldControlProps`, `FieldProps`, `FieldControlSize`, `InputProps`, `TextareaProps`, `SearchInputProps`

### File upload

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-file-upload--overview

A dropzone with a real Browse button, and a list of the files put there with their status and progress.

When to use:
- Attaching or uploading files, such as an evaluation dataset or documents for the knowledge index.
- Driving the transfer with onUpload, which queues, uploads, reports progress and retries each file.
- Stating the accepted types and the size limit before a file is chosen.

When not to:
- Attaching files to the next prompt in a conversation. Use Prompt input.
- Pasting text, such as a JSON override; a field is faster than a file. Use Textarea.

- Do: Reject a file in a sentence that names it and the rule: “budget.xlsx is 14.2 MB; the limit is 10 MB.”
- Don’t: Say “Invalid file”, or add a rejected file to the list.

Content:
- When onUpload rejects, its error message is one sentence the person can act on; it is shown under the row.
- Pass messages to translate the copy, and keep each rule stated with its figure.

#### `FileUpload` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accept` | `string` |  | Native `accept`: `.jsonl,.csv`, `application/pdf`, `image/*`. Enforced on drop as well as in the picker. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  |  |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  |  |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultFiles` | `FileUploadItem[]` |  | Rows to start with: files already on the server, or a fixed state for a demo. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `locale` | `LocalesArgument` |  | Locale for sizes and lists. Omit to use the runtime's locale. |
| `maxConcurrent` | `number` | `2` | How many `onUpload` calls run at once. |
| `maxFiles` | `number` |  | Total files in the list, including ones already there. |
| `maxSize` | `number` |  | Bytes, per file. |
| `messages` | `Partial<FileUploadMessages>` |  | Copy, for another language. Merged over the English defaults. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | Submitted with a form when there is no `onUpload`. |
| `onFilesChange` | `((files: FileUploadItem[]) => void)` |  | Every change to the list: added, progressed, finished, failed, removed. |
| `onReject` | `((rejections: FileRejection[]) => void)` |  | Files turned away, with the rule each broke. |
| `onUpload` | `((file: File, context: UploadContext) => Promise<void>)` |  | Upload one file. Resolve when done; reject with an Error whose message says why. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  |  |

#### `defaultFileUploadMessages` (constant)

#### `describeAccept` (function)

The accepted types as a person would say them — ".jsonl or .csv" — joined with the locale's own "or". MIME types are kept as written; a reader who sees `application/pdf` can still act on it, and inventing friendly names for every type is a table nobody maintains.

#### `formatFileSize` (function)

A byte count in the reader's locale: "14.2 MB", "14,2 MB", "١٤٫٢ م.ب".

#### `matchesAccept` (function)

Whether a file matches an `accept` string, using the rules the native picker uses: `.ext` against the name, `type/*` against the MIME prefix, an exact MIME type against the type. The picker's filter is advice — every platform lets the person switch it to "All files", and drag and drop skips it entirely — so the component checks again rather than trusting it.

#### `validateFiles` (function)

Splits a batch into the files that pass and the ones that do not, each with the one rule it broke. Type is checked before size, because "wrong kind of file" is the more useful thing to hear about a 2 GB video dropped on a CSV field. Count is checked last and in order, so the first files chosen are the ones kept.

Types: `FileUploadItem`, `FileUploadMessages`, `FileUploadProps`, `FileUploadStatus`, `UploadContext`, `FileRejection`, `FileRejectionReason`

### Number input

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-number-input--overview

A number you can type and step, formatted for a locale, with bounds, a unit and steppers inside the field.

When to use:
- An exact value with bounds, such as a token budget, a retry count or a timeout.
- Currency, percentages and units Intl knows, through format.
- A short unit suffix such as “tokens”, which is also added to the description.

When not to:
- A value where its place in a range matters more than the exact figure, such as temperature. Use Slider.
- An identifier made of digits, such as a run number; it is text, not a quantity. Use Input.
- A date or a period. Use Date picker.

- Do: Pass locale and a format, so “12,000 tokens” reads as a number.
- Don’t: Use a native number input, which formats nothing and changes value when the page scrolls.
- Do: Leave the wheel off in forms, and set allowWheelScrub only on a field that is the point of its screen.
- Don’t: Let scrolling past a field change its value.

Content:
- Labels name the quantity and its scope: “Token budget per run”, “Retries before halting”.
- Errors give the bound: “The workspace allows at most 8 concurrent runs.”

#### `NumberInput` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` |  | Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` |  | Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  | Defines a string value that labels the current element. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `decrementLabel` | `string` | `Decrease` |  |
| `incrementLabel` | `string` | `Increase` | Accessible names of the steppers. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Visible label above the field. Omit inside `Field`, which renders its own. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: number \| null) => void)` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
| `unit` | `string` |  | Short unit suffix inside the cut: "tokens", "ms", "%". Also added to the accessible description. |

Also accepts the props of `NumberFieldRootProps`.

Types: `NumberInputProps`

### Radio

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-radio--overview

One choice from a small set, all visible, in a named RadioGroup; square, and told from a checkbox by its mark.

When to use:
- Exactly one of two to five options that people should compare side by side.
- Options that each need a description, such as what happens when a tool call fails.

When not to:
- Any number of options. Use Checkbox.
- More options than fit comfortably, or options that do not need comparing. Use Select.
- Switching views, where the change is instant and nothing is submitted. Use Segmented control.
- A single setting that is on or off. Use Switch.

- Do: Give the group a label that asks the question: “When a tool call fails”.
- Don’t: Leave the group unnamed; a screen reader then announces “group” and nothing else.

Content:
- Option labels are parallel and start the same way: “Retry, then continue”, “Skip the step”, “Halt the run”.
- The consequence goes in description: “The run is marked failed and the owner is paged.”

#### `Radio` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |

Also accepts the props of `NativeButtonProps`, `RadioRootProps`.

#### `RadioGroup` (component)

The group, named by a visible label in the rótulo register via `aria-labelledby` — a radiogroup with no name is announced as "group" and nothing else, which leaves a screen reader user choosing between options to a question they never heard.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The question the options answer. Names the radiogroup. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` |  |

Also accepts the props of `RadioGroupProps`.

Types: `RadioGroupProps`, `RadioProps`

### Segmented control

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-segmented-control--overview

One choice from a few views or settings, all visible and switched instantly, cut from one piece.

When to use:
- Switching between views of the same content: Table, Board, Timeline.
- A setting with two to five short options that applies at once, such as density.
- Icon-only segments in a tight space, with the labels kept as accessible names.

When not to:
- More than five options, or options that need explaining. Use Select.
- A choice that is submitted with a form. Use Radio.
- Panels of different content, each with its own heading. Use Tabs.
- Filters that can be combined. Use Chip.

- Do: Always have one segment selected; pressing the selected one does nothing.
- Don’t: Use segments as a row of separate action buttons.

Content:
- Labels are one word where possible: “Table”, “Board”.
- Name the group with aria-label: “View”, “Density”.

#### `SegmentedControl` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the group. Required: three buttons reading "Table", "Board", "List" mean nothing until a screen reader hears "View". |
| `options` (required) | `SegmentedOption<V>[]` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `fill` | `boolean` | `false` | Segments share the full width equally. |
| `iconOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Render icons only; labels become the accessible names. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: V) => void)` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
| `value` | `string` |  |  |

Types: `SegmentedControlProps`, `SegmentedOption`

### Select

https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/components-forms-select--overview

A choice from a list in a popup, with an optional second line per option and labelled groups.

When to use:
- One value from a list short enough to scan without typing, such as an environment or a model.
- Options that need a second line, such as a model’s speed and cost.
- A field in a form, inside Field, or a compact filter in a toolbar.

When not to:
- A list long enough that people would rather type. Use Combobox.
- Two to five options that should all be visible. Use Radio.
- Switching views instantly. Use Segmented control.
- A list of actions rather than a value. Use Menu.

- Do: Keep a retired option in the list, disabled, with the reason as its description.
- Don’t: Remove an option someone may look for without saying where it went.

Content:
- Option labels are the names people use, “Cayuco Steady 3”; the description adds the trade-off, “Balanced · default”.
- The placeholder says what to choose: “Choose an environment”.

#### `Select` (component)

The one-line form, for the nine selects in ten that are a label and a list. The parts above are exported for the tenth.

| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | A visible label rendered above the trigger. Omit it when the select sits inside `Field`, which renders its own — and spread Field's control props onto this component instead. |
| `name` | `string` |  |  |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: V \| null) => void)` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` | `Select…` |  |
| `required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "lg" \| "md"` | `md` |  |
